text:
Starling is better if you want everything included for free, especially for travel cash, overdrafts, and depositing cash. Monzo is better if you want superior budgeting tools, social bill-splitting, or packaged bank perks (like phone/travel insurance and railcards on paid tiers).   
Abel

Both are fully licensed UK banks with FSCS protection (up to £120,000 per person) and offer fee-free debit card spending abroad at the Mastercard exchange rate.

Side-by-Side Comparison (Standard Free Accounts)
Feature	Monzo (Free Account)	Starling (Personal Account)
Monthly Fee	£0 (Paid tiers: Extra £3, Perks £7, Max £17–£19/mo)	£0 (No paid personal tiers)
Abroad ATM Withdrawals	Unlimited in EEA (if main account), £200/month outside EEA (3% fee after)	£300/day free worldwide (no monthly cap)
Depositing Cash	£1 fee per deposit at Post Office or PayPoint	Free at the Post Office (up to £1,000/year; 0.7% after)
Overdrafts	Up to £3,000 at 19%, 29%, or 39% EAR	Up to £5,000 at 15%, 25%, or 35% EAR
Budgeting & Pots	Pots with automatic Salary Sorter & bill-splitting	Spaces with virtual cards (free) & spending insights
Savings & Investing	Instant Access Pots (~2.75% AER free, higher on paid plans), Cash ISAs, & built-in Investments	Easy Saver (~2.50%–4.00% AER depending on bonus promos), Cash ISA, & 1-Year Fixed Bond
Credit / Borrowing	Monzo Flex (BNPL/credit card) & personal loans	Overdrafts only (no credit card or personal loans)
Which One Should You Pick?

Choose Starling if:

You travel frequently and use cash: The £300/day fee-free ATM limit worldwide beats Monzo's £200/month limit outside Europe without needing a paid subscription.   
Abel

You hate paywalls: Features like virtual cards (great for subscriptions and free trials) are completely free on Starling, whereas Monzo locks them behind its £3/month Extra tier.   
Abel

You handle physical cash or might use an overdraft: Post Office cash deposits are free (up to £1,000/yr), and overdraft rates are lower across the board.   
Forbes

You want a sole trader/business account: Starling's free business account is widely considered the strongest no-fee option in the UK.   
Compare the Best UK Business Bank Accounts

Choose Monzo if:

You want to automate your budgeting: Monzo's Salary Sorter automatically splits your payday money into dedicated Bills Pots, and its budgeting interface is the most intuitive on the market.   
Abel

Your friends use Monzo: Instant Monzo-to-Monzo payments, shared tabs, and bill splitting make group holidays and dinners effortless.   
Referral Plug

You want bundled extras or credit: If you already pay for a Railcard, breakdown cover, travel insurance, or phone insurance, Monzo Perks or Max can easily pay for themselves—plus you get access to Monzo Flex and in-app investing.   
Abel

A common UK hack: Because both are free to open and don't require switching your main bank, many people use Monzo for day-to-day UK spending and budgeting, and keep a Starling card specifically for holidays and overseas cash withdrawals.
